command: llvm-mc -triple=x86_64 -filetype=obj research/evidence/experiments/EXP-0052/fixture.asm -o out.o && llvm-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text out.o out.bin
notes: Eighteen EVEX vmovaps instructions with an index and a scale, one per 0.23.0 row. Each width contributes six: load and store at mod=00 (no displacement, 7 bytes), disp8*N (8 bytes) and disp32 (11 bytes), so the sizes per width are 7, 8, 11, 7, 8, 11 and the fixture is 156 bytes. The xmm six run xmm20-xmm25, the ymm six ymm9-ymm15, the zmm six zmm26-zmm31. In every row ModRM is 04/44/84 (mod 00/01/10, reg 0, r/m 100), the next byte is the SIB byte (scale at bits 7-6, index at 5-3, base at 2-0), and the displacement follows only on the 44/84 rows. A disp8*N operand carries the field content, not the byte offset: instruction 2 is 32(%rsp,%r12,2) but its plan value is 2, and instruction 17 is -8192(%rax,%rcx,1) with plan value -128; disp32 operands carry bytes. The base's fourth bit is the inverted B-bar in P0 at [13,1] (62 f1 with %rsp, 62 d1 with %r12), the index's fourth bit is the inverted X-bar at [14,1] (62 b1 with a high index such as %r12/%r13), and the vector register sits in the five-bit field at [43,3] plus the inverted R-bar/R-bar-prime bits at [12,1]/[15,1]. A displacement that is not a multiple of N promotes to disp32 (instruction 9 is 8(%rax,%rcx,1) at ymm, so N=32 and the row is 11 bytes). The fixture uses all four scale contents (0, 1, 2 and 3), base %rsp, %rbp, %r8 and %r12, and index %rax/%rcx/%rdx/%r9/%r12/%r13/%r15. input_sha256 is fixture.asm (the source above); output_sha256 is the 156-byte .text.
